FN-EJSZ892-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 34
Committee: Education Policy Sponsor: Senator Rodger Smitherman
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 02/19/2025
Senate Bill 34 as introduced, would, beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, require students
entering the ninth grade,to complete a course in violence prevention, conflict resolution, and
mediation before graduation from high school. This would increase the obligations of the State
Department of Education by an undetermined amount to: (1) prepare and make available to local
boards of education instructional materials, models, and curricula as guidelines for the
development of a violence prevention conflict resolution and meditation course or program; and
(2) assist in training teachers, to provide effective instruction in violence prevention, conflict
resolution and meditation.
Additionally, this bill would increase the administrative obligations of: (1) the local boards of
education to determine the appropriate curriculum to satisfy the requirements of this bill; and (2)
the State Board of Education to adopt rules to implement the provisions of this bill.

FN-EJSZ892-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 34
Committee: Education Policy Sponsor: Senator Rodger Smitherman
Analyst: John Friedenreich Date: 04/29/2025
Senate Bill 34 as passed the Senate, would, beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, require
students entering middle school,to complete a course in violence prevention, conflict resolution,
and mediation before promotion to high school. This would increase the obligations of the State
Department of Education by an undetermined amount dependent on the cost to: (1) prepare and
make available to local boards of education instructional materials, models, and curricula as
guidelines for the development of a violence prevention conflict resolution and meditation
course or program; and (2) assist in training teachers, to provide effective instruction in violence
prevention, conflict resolution and meditation.
Additionally, this bill would increase the administrative obligations of: (1) the local boards of
education to determine the appropriate curriculum to satisfy the requirements of this bill; and (2)
the State Board of Education to adopt rules to implement the provisions of this bill.
